feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector positioning is consistent. It reads polished and modern, though it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that slightly reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative: progression within NACo is logical and supports the “digital platform & communications systems leader” positioning.  
- Good use of scale and credibility signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms, and concrete project examples.  
- Broad but coherent skill set spanning strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and project descriptions; consolidate to create a tighter, more scannable CV.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond scope metrics: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, or campaign performance.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs “organization’s,” mixed punctuation in bullets, and serial comma inconsistency (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs lists without final comma). Minor wording issue: “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary and weakens the education section. No obvious misspellings; grammar is generally strong.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to enterprise/public-sector digital transformation.
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase impact.
- Tighten the list of responsibilities into fewer, sharper themes: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Consider rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Led a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled search experiences” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is close to the subtitle and skills sections; avoid repeating all three elsewhere verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this section overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership”
- Replace broader items with more specific, senior-level language: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”; “Workflow automation and platform integration” is strong and current
- Consider “Public-sector advocacy communications” for cleaner phrasing than “Advocacy and public-sector communications”
- Revised version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header and Topline Skills; consider trimming either this section or the Topline Skills categories
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also repeats strongly across Work Experience and Technical + IT
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and making outcomes or scope clearer will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a concise 1-line achievement for easier scanning.
- Use parallel verbs and cleaner phrasing: “Created AI-powered legislative search combining hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Clarify audience/value where possible: “to help users navigate complex policy content” or “to support ongoing campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style and wording: change “10×20-foot” to “10 x 20-foot” for consistency; consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” throughout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item here; prioritize unique projects or add outcomes to avoid this section feeling repetitive.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives to make it feel more senior and distinct from the NACo entries.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, and coordinated communications operations.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one stronger line: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Split out the most distinctive technical work: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery design.” Add metrics if possible: launch status, content volume, traffic, time saved, or engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “enterprise web improvement” overlap with the Director of Digital Media role; keep this entry focused on consulting impact and current initiatives.
- The microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep one high-level here and let the project section carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were more concise and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team/operational scope, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channels/results more specific: add email list size, engagement growth, campaign performance, or follower growth if available; otherwise trim to avoid generic “tens of thousands/thousands.”
- Strengthen outcome language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring video series”; “Expanded analytics stack… enabling executive reporting and better channel/content decisions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video, newsletters, and editorial coordination overlap with the 2018–2022 NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- The Drupal microsite/project details are already reinforced in Recent Projects, so avoid overloading this item with similar build-level detail.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. It should emphasize what you owned at this level—operational leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination—without repeating broader platform/governance claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletters, advocacy video series, cross-functional editorial planning, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: open/click rates, subscriber growth, video cadence/views, turnaround time, number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Example phrasing: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this entry as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector specialization rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and operationally grounded.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague; “audience strategy and content planning” is stronger and more executive-level.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: governance, enterprise web, and cross-channel operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also duplicates the header and multiple recent roles; keep only if this is a target-market keyword.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skills, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older platforms unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages from this topline line.
- Cut “jQuery” unless specifically requested in job descriptions; it dates the profile and adds little strategic value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to connect with the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; use Topline Skills for themes, not a second software inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a duplicate of the “Technical + IT” analytics section and misses the leadership/decision-making angle that better fits a topline skills block. Shift from software inventory to higher-value capability framing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Lead with capabilities, then tools; this better matches seniority and avoids sounding like a technical checklist.
- Replace “optimization” with clearer outcomes language if possible, e.g. “insight generation” or “decision support,” unless you can point to testing/CRO elsewhere.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “cross-channel performance reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list in both Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior, selective, and tied to the strongest recent/most credible capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, higher-level phrasing: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems”
- Drop “video production and editing” if editing is not a differentiator at your current senior level; “broadcast video production” signals more scope.
- Consider adding scale/context if space allows: “for advocacy, executive, and member-facing programming”
- Keep to 4 items max and use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing tools (“PTZ camera systems”) with formats (“hybrid and virtual event production”) unless standardized as “PTZ/multi-camera production systems” and “hybrid event delivery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- Studio/video capability is also evidenced in NACo roles, so this section should summarize, not repeat detail.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating names only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding version/scope only where strongest: **Drupal 10** or **Drupal (10,000+ page migration)** if consistent with the rest of the CV.
- Keep this item platform-focused; avoid adding HTML/CSS/API language here since that’s already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider trimming one or making this version more specific to platform depth.
- GitHub Pages may read as lightweight compared with the enterprise/public-sector emphasis; remove if not materially relevant.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the more current tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API and tag implementation • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value.
- Group related items to show capability, not just tools: “API and tag implementation” is stronger than separate fragmented keywords.
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end implementation for Drupal-based sites” or “deployment automation,” to connect this list to current experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing either this item or the overlapping Topline Skills line to avoid repetition.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems-building, not just apps: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Remove Basecamp unless it was used recently or materially; it weakens recency and focus.
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project workflows: Jira, Asana, Trello | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Best upgrade: replace this list with outcome-oriented wording elsewhere, e.g., “Built workflow automation and cross-team planning systems using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack and Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if central to workflow/system design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Reorder by likely strategic relevance/enterprise weight: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member communications/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)
- Keep formatting parallel with other technical items; avoid slashes if possible for readability: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; keep this item tool-focused only.
- “Engagement” may blur with broader communications leadership already covered in Core Competencies; “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” is clearer.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of capability. Tighten it into a cleaner technical stack and use more precise labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing) • Executive dashboard reporting
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “Executive dashboard reporting” or “KPI reporting” to sound more outcome-oriented.
- Replace plain “SEO” with “SEO analysis” or “SEO performance analysis” to better match your strategic/measurement focus.
- Keep only platforms and methods here; if space allows elsewhere, quantify impact in experience bullets instead of this skills line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider removing one section or making this one tools-only and the other strategy-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup for later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific, while avoiding overlap with the 2018–2024 entries on newsletters, advocacy video, and digital operations leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving production workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream frequency, video cadence, audience growth, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked clauses: split team-building, website refresh, content production, and supervision into distinct outcomes.
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and streamline multi-channel production workflows. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video content, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as early production/build-out.
- “strengthening workflows” is close to later operations/governance language; frame this as foundational process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb, e.g., “produced” or “supported multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audiences served, internal teams supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy or member engagement.
- Keep this entry to one concise sentence or two short clauses since later roles already show broader digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating general digital content/multimedia language covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; save management/operations emphasis for 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it mixes software with capabilities and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Tightening it to named tools only will make it cleaner and less repetitive.
